propositions: The blocking-link resolver derives comparability from a ticket's type tier instead of its position in the parent hierarchy, silently recording a different edge than requested.
A ticket can end up with a blocking edge against its own ancestor or descendant, distorting ready, next-batch, and the parent-first claim cascade.
Comparability should be structural (nearest-common-ancestor): any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a direct dependency regardless of type.
No blocking edge should be representable between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant by any path into the resolver.
Blocking edges already written under the old type-tier rule must be detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass via link-audit.
Auto-escalation of cross-subtree links and its machine-readable redirect record must remain unchanged for existing callers.
